title: Precision Allocations: field-validation playbook for prefetched caching and lightweight quant profiles
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Run a targeted initiative to validate workload-specific savings from combining selective KV-prefetching with low-loss quant profiles and request-level allocation policies. Goal is a repeatable playbook and validation harness that PMs and Eng field teams can run against customer traffic slices to measure net token-cost reduction while preserving 99th%-tile latency SLOs and core output quality metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook documented with step-by-step run instructions, parameters, and decision thresholds
Validation harness (scripts + dashboards) can run on a representative scorecard slice and produce cost + quality delta report within 48 hours
At least three customer or internal workload slices validated showing >=15% cost/unit savings without >1% degradation in top-level eval metrics
Auto-rollback criteria defined and tested (quality regression >1% or P99 latency exceedance)
Integration checklist completed: tagging for experiments in Console, metric capture for cost, latency, and quality, and one-click rollback in canary
tasks: Define experiment matrix: workloads, quant profiles (int8-lite, int8-aggressive), prefetch TTLs, and batching windows
Build validation harness: runner, metric collector, and report generator
Instrument Console: per-route cost delta chart, quality regression alerts, and canary rollback hook
Coordinate Eng teams for kernel/quant profile toggles in runtime-1.19
Run 2-week internal field trials on 3 distinct workload families (search, chat assistants, single-turn generation)
Document playbook and publish to Confluence + link in Console experiment UI
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Mehta (PM): Created ticket. Hypothesis: selective KV-prefetch + conservative int8-lite quant yields steady token-cost savings for assistant workloads with long context reuse.
2025-02-17 - Liam O'Connor (PM): Scoped matrix and drafted initial acceptance criteria. Eng ask: require runtime flags for 'prefetch-policy-v2' and 'quant-lite'. Opened ENG-50432 to implement flags.

2025-02-21 - Priya Shah (Eng): Implemented metric export endpoints for per-request cache-hit and quant-profile tags. Deployed to staging. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892
2025-02-25 - Jun Park (Design): Added UI mockups for the 'Experiment run' page in Console. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/prefetch-playbook-v1

2025-03-01 - Liam O'Connor (PM): First internal run completed on 'assistant-small' slice. Preliminary results: 12% token-cost savings, 0.6% drop on BLEU-like eval. Decided to try slightly more conservative quant thresholds and longer KV TTL for next run.

2025-03-04 - Priya Shah (Eng): Deployed int8-lite variant and longer KV TTL toggle to canary. Added automated rollback hook for P99 latency. See GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/734
notes: Risk: aggressive quantization can create subtle semantic regressions for instruction-following models; include prompt-specific evals in harness
Plan to expose a 'confidence band' in the report that combines quality and latency to make trade-offs explicit for product owners
Next checkpoint: 2025-03-18 review with Reliability and Customer Success to align on rollout guardrails
